title: INT8 weight-only: stability sweep, calibration reconciliation, and regression harness
creator: Leah Park
description: Integrate INT8 weight-only quantization profiles produced by GPTQ/AWQ into the calibration and regression pipelines, verify stability across model families and prompt distributions, and implement a nightly harness that detects accuracy regressions and calibration drift. This ticket focuses on end-to-end validation and operational playbooks: producing reproducible calibration artifacts, running a staged stability sweep, defining pass/fail thresholds, and wiring automated alerts and rollback triggers for canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration artifacts from GPTQ and AWQ can be ingested by the profile registry and mapped to model-version metadata (schema v2) without manual intervention
Nightly stability sweep runs for the target model families (base-13B, chat-30B, and embed-3B) and produces a report with accuracy deltas vs the FP16 golden baseline
Regression guardrails: no more than 1.5% relative drop in Rouge-L or 2% increase in perplexity (dataset-specific threshold) for any model variant in the sweep
Canary gating: if any model variant exceeds threshold, the canary rollout is blocked and the rollback playbook is triggered automatically
Telemetry emitted for each run: profile_id, model_version, prompt_set_id, median_latency_ms, tokens_generated, accuracy_metric_name, accuracy_delta, job_id
Runbook documented and linked; on-call runbook tested once in synthetic failure injection
plan_steps: Map GPTQ/AWQ output files to quant-profile schema v2 and add metadata extraction hooks in profile-registry service
Add ingestion unit tests and a small adapter in model-onboarding to normalize scales and group-wise quant params
Create a nightly orchestration job (k8s CronJob) that executes the stability sweep across the golden prompt sets in parallel with resource-aware batching
Implement evaluation harness that computes multiple metrics (perplexity, Rouge-L, Exact Match, embedding cosine) and aggregates deltas against FP16 golden runs
Add transient-canary feature flag and pipeline integration: automatically block canaries when thresholds fail and post results to #quant-regressions and Alerts
Write rollback playbook with steps to revert model routing, invalidate profile cache, and schedule a manual calibration re-run
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use nightly sweep cadence (vs hourly) because end-to-end calibration runs are resource intensive and nightly provides stable signal while limiting cost
Tradeoff: We will run a reduced prompt set for the largest models (chat-30B) to bound GPU time; full prompt set runs are retained for smaller models
Decision: Treat AWQ and GPTQ profiles as independent variants with separate profile_ids rather than attempting to merge parameters; simplifies rollback and A/B comparison
Tradeoff: Tighter accuracy thresholds increase false positives; chosen thresholds bias towards preventing customer regressions at the cost of occasional manual triage
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting; aligned on schema changes for profile-registry v2. Action: ENG infra to provide a 4-node ephemeral GPU pool for nightly runs (assigned ENG-26300).
2026-02-20: Prototype adapter that maps AWQ metadata to the profile schema completed (PR #12418). Initial local runs show <1% perplexity delta on a 1k prompt subset.
2026-02-28: Integration tests added to CI for ingestion; discovered edge case where quant scale arrays have variable length for layer-norm layers — added normalization step in adapter.
2026-03-04: Nightly CronJob skeleton deployed to staging; running stability sweep against embed-3B with reduced prompt set; perf telemetry hooks in place.
2026-03-09: First staging sweep flagged one AWQ variant with 3.2% Rouge-L drop vs FP16 on summarization set. Follow-up: created ENG-27510 to triage AWQ calibration hyperparams.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Noisy signal from small prompt sets can cause spurious failures. Mitigation: use bootstrap aggregation and require failure across 2 consecutive nightly runs to trigger canary block.
Risk: Large models consume significant GPU time. Mitigation: limit per-model budget and sample prompts using stratified stratagem across token length and domain.
Risk: Schema mismatch with older profiles breaks ingestion. Mitigation: implement compatibility shim that rejects unknown fields and logs telemetry for manual inspection.
Risk: Emergency rollback may cause brief traffic blip. Mitigation: implement gradual traffic shift with canary rollback using traffic-split API and monitor latency SLOs during rollback
telemetry_requirements: Emit profile_id, profile_variant (GPTQ|AWQ), model_family, model_version in every job event
Record metric buckets for accuracy (mean, median, 90th percentile) and raw per-prompt deltas for later drilldown
Log resource usage: GPU-hours, memory-allocations, and peak KV-cache size for each profile test
Push summarized results to observability dashboard (dashboard id: quant-stability-v2) and post alerts for failures
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for profile adapter and schema validation (coverage target 95%)
End-to-end staging sweep against canonical FP16 golden runs with seeded RNG for deterministic reproducibility
Failure-injection run: corrupt a scale array to validate that ingestion rejects bad profiles and triggers alert
Canary rollout simulation in staging where the canary is expected to be blocked if thresholds are exceeded
runbook_snippet: 1) If nightly sweep fails: verify telemetry and rerun the failing profile with --deterministic-seed
2) If failure reproduces: block canary via feature flag and notify #quant-regressions with summary and link to artifact
3) Follow triage checklist: compare per-layer scale histograms, compare AWQ vs GPTQ, decide: re-calibrate / reject profile / fallback to FP16
4) Escalation: if customer-impacting, open a high-priority incident and notify product and TPMs
notes: Make sure calibration outputs store random seeds and PyTorch cudnn flags so runs are reproducible across hosts.
We should later extend the harness for FP8 experiments; scaffolding now should be flexible to add FP8 profiles
Coordinate with SRE to reserve preemptible GPU pool for nightly runs to reduce cost; ensure fallback to on-demand if preempted
